claims.text: A machine-learning-driven computational design tool can identify automotive exhaust catalyst formulations with improved catalytic activity relative to conventionally developed catalysts.
Machine-learning-designed formulations can improve catalyst durability relative to conventionally developed catalysts.
Machine-learning-designed formulations can reduce PGM consumption relative to conventionally developed catalysts.
The computational framework can predict catalyst formulations that minimize PGM content while enhancing catalyst microstructure and performance.
The computationally selected formulations will produce enhanced nanoparticle-support interfaces.
The computationally selected formulations will optimize metal dispersion.
Enhanced nanoparticle-support interfaces and optimized metal dispersion will produce a more robust catalyst structure.
Enhanced nanoparticle-support interfaces and optimized metal dispersion will reduce catalyst sintering.
An optimal balance of support materials and alloying elements improves active-site accessibility.
An optimal balance of support materials and alloying elements improves active-site stability.
Increasing the effective utilization of catalytic sites reduces the amount of PGM required.
Mitigating sintering during high-temperature operation improves catalyst durability.
Computationally designed catalysts will exhibit approximately 15–20% improved catalytic activity relative to conventionally designed catalysts.
Computationally designed catalysts will exhibit approximately 15–20% improved durability relative to conventionally designed catalysts.
Computationally designed catalysts will reduce PGM consumption by approximately 25–30% relative to conventionally designed catalysts.
The predicted improvements will hold under typical automotive operating conditions and within the synthesis limits of the proposed support materials.
Variations in real-world operating conditions or synthesis challenges may affect catalyst performance.
Model prediction variability and synthesis reproducibility create uncertainty in the magnitude of the anticipated improvements.
